newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jury convicts Tyson Foods lobbyist of lying.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jury convicts Tyson Foods lobbyist of lying.

text.p: A federal court jury convicted Tyson Foods Inc. lobbyist Jack Williams on Friday on two counts of lying during an investigation of former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.

Jurors returned the verdict after about three hours of deliberations. Sentencing was set for June 5. Williams faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine but his lawyers have said under sentencing guidelines he might serve no more than six months, possibly on probation.
Defence attorney Barry Levine said he would file a motion asking U.S. District Judge James Robertson to set aside the verdict. If that failed, an appeal was likely, he said.
"We think the verdict is wrong. It is not supported by the evidence," Levine said. "This is not a case the Justice Department would have brought."
Charges stemmed from an investigation headed by independent counsel Donald Smaltz.

Espy resigned in 1994 amid allegations he improperly accepted gifts from businesses that his department regulated. Investigators said Williams tried to mislead them about his role in Espy's attendance at a pro football game as a Tyson Foods guest and in helping Espy's girlfriend get a scholarship from Tyson Foundation.
